human_reviews.note: בתשובה האמיתית הם שילבו בין פתרון 2 סעיפים (5 ו-6). האמירה היחידה שחסרה היא שהמסכה גאוסיאנית, אבל נראה שהייתה הבנה של הפעולה

errors.rationale: The whole answer is one clause: "מריחה בציר x עקב הקונבולוציה". It states exactly the core of the official solution for operation 5 ("טשטוש התמונה בכוון אופקי") but omits everything else — the Gaussian 1-D mask identity, the noise, and the consequence that the vertical edges ("השפות האנכיות") are affected. Instructor (2.0), Or Vaisman, and the adjudicated reference all landed on partial; Erik (medium confidence) said valid and explicitly flagged issue=rubric_official_solution, noting the only missing statement is that the mask is Gaussian ("האמירה היחידה שחסרה היא שהמסכה גאוסיאנית"). This is a genuine full-vs-partial boundary on a terse but core-correct answer, and the model fell on the generous side of it; nothing was credited that is absent, so this is not model_too_generous. The generic rubric ("8 פעולות ו-9 היסטוגרמות") gives no full-vs-partial criteria, which is what leaves the boundary soft.
errors.model_evidence_assessment: The cited span "מריחה בציר x עקב הקונבולוציה" is the student's entire 28-char answer verbatim, so the evidence exists and genuinely supports the met=true finding for the directional-blur core claim. It does not, however, establish anything beyond that single claim, so it supports partial credit well and full credit only weakly — the evidence is real but overweighted.

The readable remainder "כולם משומשים בכמות יחסית אחידה" is genuinely two-faced: it can be read as the wrong 'uniform bins' answer (the UQ trap) or as the correct OQ consequence that dense regions get small bins so every bin carries similar pixel mass. Reviewer Or Vaisman voted partially_valid and explicitly flagged issue=transcription_evidence; Erik voted invalid at LOW confidence with the note "נראה לי הפוך מהשתובה, אבל בדירוג המקורי נתנו ניקוד מלא" (seems inverted, yet the instructor gave full credit, 4.0). With the decisive words garbled, the model's 0-credit read is best explained by the degraded evidence rather than a clean invalid-vs-partial judgment error; the adjudication (partially_valid, empty note, over a split low/high-confidence panel) is itself thin, but the transcription gaps are the root cause.
errors.model_evidence_assessment: The cited span exists in the student text (it is the transcription minus the leading "[לא קריא]") and is quoted faithfully, including an embedded "[לא קריא]" marker — i.e. the model graded over admittedly garbled evidence. The span does not decisively support met=false: the readable clause admits a partial-credit reading (uniform per-bin usage, consistent with OQ) that the not-met call cannot rule out given the gaps.

errors.question: q2

errors.rationale: Canny question; official solution requires a binary image: 255 at detected edge pixels AND 0 everywhere else (וערכי 0 בכל השאר). The student wrote "כל פיקסלי השפות שנקלטו קיבלו ערך 255 לעומת שאר הפיקסלים(הרוב)" — edges get 255 versus the rest (the majority) — nailing the 255-edge half and implying a contrast, but never stating the rest are 0 / that the output is binary. Both blind reviewers gave partially_valid (consensus reference), while the instructor gave full credit, and Erik's note explicitly wavers: "כנראה שזה פרט לא מהותי?" (perhaps a non-essential detail?). This is a textbook full-vs-partial boundary: the model's charitable full credit is defensible (the instructor agreed), it simply landed on the wrong side of a genuinely close completeness line.
errors.model_evidence_assessment: The cited span is verbatim the whole student answer and genuinely supports met=true for the edges-get-255 element. It does not, however, contain the 'zeros elsewhere / binary' element, so it supports at most partial-to-full credit depending on where the completeness bar sits; the model's valid verdict overreads the span relative to the human consensus. Flags: rubric gives no per-item breakdown saying whether '0 elsewhere' is required (Erik's note questions exactly this, and the instructor credited fully), and the reference rests on a 2-0 consensus where one review is low-confidence and contradicts the instructor.
